description: Stored exposure is an inclusive day count (25 to 365) instead of a year fraction in a small cluster of training rows of all three lines; stored / date-derived exposure sits at exactly 365. None in the test files.
action_detail: exposure replaced by (period_end - period_start + 1) / 365 for every policy and test row (114 day-count rows: motor 47, buildings 33, contents 34). Total training exposure moves from 127,105 to 91,495 exposure-years; test exposure is unchanged beyond rounding.
rationale: The inclusive-days convention is confirmed by the ~1 cluster matching (days+1)/365 to 4 dp on 99.3% of rows and on 100% of test rows; dividing by 365 maps every day-count row into the normal range. Left as delivered these rows would carry 365x weight in the offset.

description: A second exposure convention hides behind the day-count cluster: rows whose stored exposure equals days / 360 (ratio to the date-derived value 1.0139, up to 5 days of exposure too much on a full year). Present in 2023 and 2024 of all three lines, absent from the test files.
action_detail: Repaired by the same uniform recomputation from the period dates as F-EXP-DAYS (494 rows: motor 207, buildings 121, contents 166). Effect on total exposure is about +0.4 exposure-years per line, i.e. immaterial to levels, but the cluster is recorded because it proves the stored column mixes conventions.
rationale: R-0014: tabulating stored / derived showed a cluster at 365/360 exactly, not rounding noise (rounding noise is below 0.0001). All rows are recomputed from dates so no convention survives.

description: sum_insured recorded 1,000x too large on a cluster of buildings and contents rows in both training and test files (values 1e7..6e8 against a normal range of 4e4..9e5 for buildings and 5e3..3e5 for contents). The written_premium / sum_insured ratio of these rows sits three decades below the line median.
action_detail: sum_insured divided by 1,000 where written_premium / sum_insured < (line median ratio) / 10. Rows: policies_buildings 53, test_buildings 104, policies_contents 57, test_contents 135. Boundary decision: per table the log10 of the ratio relative to its median is never below -0.36 for ordinary rows and never above -1.97 for the error cluster, so any cut between -0.5 and -1.9 separates them; one decade below the median was chosen as a round number inside the gap. A value threshold (SI > 2e6) selects the same rows but a ratio rule needs no tuned number and was applied unchanged to all four tables. After repair the rescaled values fall inside the normal range (buildings 73,000..470,000; contents 7,600..131,600).
rationale: R-0003/R-0013: a mass exactly three decades off is a unit error, not a large risk; premium is on the normal scale so sum_insured is the wrong column. Test rows carry the same defect, so leaving them would corrupt those predictions directly.

description: Content-key duplicate check on claims (policy_id, peril, loss_date, paid, incurred, recoveries): no exact copies under a different claim_id. Also none on (policy_id, peril, loss_date) alone. Negative result recorded for the audit trail (the developed market had such duplicates).
action_detail: Check run on the as-delivered claims table; 0 duplicates; nothing removed.
rationale: R-0002 asks for the check and for the negative result to be recorded.

description: 36 claims (of 9258) have a loss_date earlier than every policy period of their policy_id (14+ days before the first row; loss years {'loss_date': [2021, 2022, 2023], 'count': [6, 28, 2]}); the other 9222 link to exactly one row by loss date (99.6%). Their report lags are 411..565 days against a matched-claim p99 of 241 days, so they fail the R-0015 lag-plausibility test. 31 of the 36 belong to policies that also appear in the 2025 test file.
action_detail: Removed from outputs/cleaned/claims.parquet. Incurred removed 97,099.25 CU = 0.33% of total incurred (net non-repudiated 92,267.26). By line: {'line': ['buildings', 'contents', 'motor'], 'len': [3, 5, 28]}. They cannot contribute to any row target because no row covers their loss date, so the modelling target is unaffected either way; the exclusion keeps the cleaned claims table reconcilable to the policy rows. Listed in work/excluded_claims.parquet.
rationale: R-0004/R-0015: a loss before the policy's first row is a date or linkage defect, not a late report; re-dating would invent information. The share of incurred is bounded (0.3%) so the effect on levels is negligible. A human should confirm whether these are pre-inception claims from the acquired broker book or mis-keyed loss dates.

description: 27 linked claims each exceed 2% of their line-year net incurred: buildings fire losses of 110k..361k CU (the largest is 9.7% of buildings 2024), buildings and contents flood losses, and two motor bodily-injury claims of 137k and 156k. Buildings fire is 13 of them and carries 45% of buildings cost from 6.6% of its claims.
action_detail: Kept unchanged in the cleaned claims table. Handed to target construction (cap at a high quantile of positive row targets and redistribute the excess as a line-level multiplier, R-0104) and excluded from the completion curve fit by capping (R-0102). Mentioned wherever buildings 2023 vs 2024 or emerging vs developed severity is compared.
rationale: R-0008: one such claim changes the buildings year level by 5-10%; deletion would bias the level, so they are flagged, not removed.

description: Latest loss_date 2024-12-29, latest report_date 2024-12-30, no report before loss, no claim in the 2025 test period: consistent with the stated 31 December 2024 valuation. December 2024 has 268 reported losses against a 2024 monthly mean of about 400, the expected last-month under-reporting (R-0106). 2024 open share is 20% of motor claims and 25% of buildings claims against 4% for 2023, so 2024 is materially incomplete.
action_detail: No change to data. Carried into target construction: completion (IBNR) curve as an offset, open-claim adequacy check, and the warning that 2024 rows must not be compared raw with 2023.
rationale: R-0007 asks for the valuation check and an estimate of how much of the latest accident year is outstanding.

description: renewal_decision is recorded at the end of the policy period (renewed / lapsed / cancelled / mid_term_change / declined_by_insurer) and is absent from the test files. Rows declined by the insurer carry 1.14 claims per row against 0.09 overall, so the column encodes the outcome.
action_detail: Column kept in the cleaned training tables (schema parity) but excluded from every feature set; the 'mid_term_change' value is used only to mark the first row of a two-row policy year for the R-0309 bias check.
rationale: Post-period information that does not exist at pricing time (R-0005); the test files do not carry it.

description: customer_service_contacts is mechanically tied to claims: rows with 0 contacts have 0 claims, rows with 2 contacts 0.26 claims, with 5+ contacts more than one claim per row. Its upper tail exists only in training (max 20 vs 5 in test; mean 0.8 vs 0.4 for motor).
action_detail: Kept in the cleaned tables; excluded from all feature sets in the modelling tables (flagged as a data-quality/leakage marker, not a risk factor).
rationale: R-0005: a behaviour count accumulated during the period whose value grows with the claims it would predict is not available at pricing time in the same form.

description: customer_since_year is a cohort stamp: it equals the policy inception year exactly (policy year minus customer_since_year equals renewal_count on 100% of training policy-years), and 99,088 of 135,856 customers carry the value 2025, which only test rows can have. A single-feature adversarial AUC of 0.8+ separates 2024 training rows from test rows on it.
action_detail: Kept in the cleaned customers table; excluded from features. Tenure information is taken from renewal_count, which carries the identical content with the same meaning in both years.
rationale: R-0016/R-0006: a deterministic function of join year is a time stamp, not a risk factor.

description: campaign_code nullness is a deterministic function of join year: 74.6% null for customers who joined before 2025 and 0% null for the 2025 (test-only) cohort, so the null level alone identifies training rows.
action_detail: Kept in the cleaned customers table; excluded from features (the codes themselves are uniform across 15 values and carry no visible risk signal).
rationale: R-0016: a null pattern that exists only before a system or campaign existed is a time stamp.

description: discount_applied is a deterministic function of channel and new_business (0.05 if and only if channel = direct; 0.10 if and only if channel = comparison_site and new_business; else 0). The 0.10 level is 0.7% of training rows but 3.8% of test rows because the test year is mostly new business.
action_detail: Kept; dropped from the lean feature set as redundant with channel x new_business.
rationale: Found by cross-tabulating columns during profiling; not a defect, but a redundant column would be read as a separate risk factor.

description: occupation has 81 distinct raw values for 20 job titles: 25% of non-null values are lower-cased, 15% carry a trailing space and 10% carry a 'Self-employed ' prefix. The prefix rate is 10% for every title including 'retired', 'student' and 'unemployed', so it is a random corruption, not a recorded attribute. The developed market records the same 20 titles cleanly.
action_detail: 59899 values normalised to the 20 canonical titles (strip whitespace, remove the prefix, canonical case); nulls untouched (16,517). The customers table serves train and test rows alike.
rationale: Without normalisation the model sees 'Retired', 'retired' and 'Retired ' as three segments; the uniform prefix rate rules out real information in 'Self-employed'.

description: flood_zone is null on 2.9% of addresses and the nulls are not at random: null addresses sit a median 1.15 km from a river at 4.4 m elevation (zone-2/3 territory) against 3.3 km and 10 m for zone 1, and their buildings claim frequency is about twice that of non-null addresses (0.065 vs 0.031; contents 0.041 vs 0.026).
action_detail: Left null in the cleaned table; carried into the modelling tables as its own 'unknown' level (never imputed to the mode).
rationale: R-0018: a null group that differs systematically from non-null rows carries risk information.

description: Fifteen attribute columns across customers, addresses and the policy/test tables are null on 11.8-12.3% of rows each. The nulls are independent draws: co-occurrence within a row follows the binomial expectation, the null share is the same in train and test, across channels, new-business status and regions, and claim frequency in the null group matches the non-null group within noise (unlike flood_zone).
action_detail: No imputation. Nulls are passed to the models as a missing value / 'unknown' category; no missing-indicator features are created.
rationale: R-0018: nulls that look like independent draws need no indicator; imputing to the mode would only blur the known levels.

description: Every 2023 policy (20,084 motor, 12,107 buildings, 14,982 contents) reappears in 2024, and no 2023 row carries a lapsed or cancelled renewal_decision, while 2024 shows 15% of policies lapsing or cancelling before 2025. The 2023 year therefore contains only policies that survived into 2024: it is a survivor-biased sample, 2024 is not.
action_detail: No row removed. Recorded for the shift report and validation design: the 2023 -> 2024 time fold trains on survivors only; the 2023 burning cost may understate the cost of a complete book if lapsing policies differ in risk (lapsed/cancelled 2024 rows show 0.05 claims per row against 0.09 for renewed rows, mostly an exposure effect).
rationale: Found by checking persistence of policies year to year. The team should confirm whether the extract was built from policies in force at end-2024 (looking back) or whether 2023 lapses were dropped.

description: Policy rows are calendar-year slices: no row crosses a year end; a policy has one row per year or two when a mid-term change occurred (the second row carries the new vehicle or address). 2024 rows end on 2024-12-30, 2023 and 2025 rows on 12-31, so every year has 365 covered days and exposure 1.0 means 365 days; no claim falls on 2024-12-30/31.
action_detail: No change; the inclusive-days / 365 exposure definition is applied uniformly. Mid-term second rows are kept as separate rows (they carry different risk attributes) and flagged in the modelling tables for the R-0309 bias check.
rationale: Documenting the row convention is needed to reproduce exposure and to link claims by loss date.

description: reference_policies holds 20 rows that are cell-for-cell copies of 20 rows of the 2025 test files (7 motor, 7 buildings, 6 contents; 18 broker new business), in a single wide schema with numeric columns typed float because of cross-line nulls. It adds no information; it is a reference subset for the premium build / sanity checks.
action_detail: Copied through unchanged. Its sum_insured and exposure values are on the normal scale; predictions for these 20 row_ids come from the test files.
rationale: Found by matching row_ids; recorded so nobody treats it as extra training data.

description: expenses has no emerging-market value for commission_comparison_site (null) although the comparison_site channel writes 5% of training rows and 5% of test rows in every line. All other items are present (fixed expense 85 CU, variable 15%, broker commission 20%, premium tax 8%, cat reinsurance 12% of property risk premium, profit margin 8%).
action_detail: Left null, copied through. Not filled: the premium build for comparison-site business cannot be completed until the team supplies the loading (the developed-market value is 10%).
rationale: R-0412: every channel in the book needs an entry; a missing entry is a team query, not something to fill in silently.

description: weather carries 2025 values for every address (the prediction year), and the 2025 means differ from 2023-24 (hail days 11.4 vs 14-17, freezing days 28.9 vs 17-21, rainfall 1,251 vs 1,378 mm). Within-address year-to-year variation is large, so the values are year-specific, not a climate normal. The emerging market is also warmer and wetter than the developed one (15.1 vs 12.6 C, 1,336 vs 1,040 mm, hail 14 vs 6 days).
action_detail: Copied through. Weather variables are left out of the lean feature set (Part 1 found year-varying weather did not transfer out of year, R-0302) and may be tested as a group under the validation rule.
rationale: Year-specific values whose 2025 realisation could not be known at pricing time; whether they are forecasts or realised values is unstated.

description: For customers holding more than one line in the same year the age band disagrees between lines in 262 of 79,886 customer-years (0.3%), always by one adjacent band; year-on-year the band moves 0 or +1 only. Consistent with a birthday between two inception dates, not an identity error.
action_detail: No change; each line keeps its own band.
rationale: Cross-table consistency check run during profiling; the rate and direction are what a banded age would produce.

description: ncb_years exceeds years_licensed on 16% of motor training rows and 22% of motor test rows (a driver cannot have more no-claims years than licence years). Age band and years_licensed are mutually consistent (17-24 never above 7 years), so ncb_years is the suspect column. The same share in train and test says it is a systematic recording convention, not a cohort effect.
action_detail: Both columns kept unchanged (no basis to choose which is wrong); a flag is carried in the modelling table. The team should confirm how ncb_years is defined in this market (it may include years earned elsewhere or be a transferred rating step rather than a count of years).
rationale: Repairing would require assuming which column is right; the pattern is uniform across train and test so the model sees the same convention in both.

description: customers carries gender (emerging only; the developed market has none). Motor claim frequency differs materially by gender within age bands (17-24: men 0.354 vs women 0.210; 25-34: 0.228 vs 0.163). Whether gender may be used as a rating factor in this market is a regulatory question the data cannot answer.
action_detail: Kept in the cleaned table. Left out of the baseline feature set pending a team decision; the frequency differential is documented so the cost of excluding it is known.
rationale: R-0404 default stance is to re-estimate relativities on emerging data, but a rating factor that may be prohibited must be a human decision.
